To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a scalable neural architecture with a shared multi-layer encoder, a novel personalized attention mechanism and domain-specific classifiers, that efficiently solves the problem of mapping spoken language to thousands of natural language domains in IPDAs.

1) a shared encoder and personalized attention can be used to achieve state-of-the-art accuracy on the domain classification task, and 2) the architecture is scalable to thousands of overlapping domains and can be incrementally updated as new domains are added to the system.
(a) a neural model that incorporates personalization improves domain classification accuracy, and (b) our proposed architecture can be trained efficiently to accommodate incremental domain additions.

we have proposed a scalable and efficient neural architecture for spoken language understanding that incorporates personalization and can accommodate incremental domain additions.

our proposed architecture is able to achieve a 10.3% absolute improvement in domain classification accuracy compared to a baseline system, while achieving a 10x reduction in training time, a 2x reduction in memory footprint, and a 10x increase in inference throughput.

personalization is a powerful signal for domain classification, and that a scalable model architecture with a novel attention mechanism and a shared encoder is able to efficiently utilize this information to improve domain classification performance.
